title: IR signal triage and SIEM export procedures
summary: Concise on-call procedures for triaging signals, mapping RBAC v2 contexts, and exporting evidentiary artifacts to SIEM/forensics with automated hooks. Focus is on fast signal enrichment, guaranteed chain-of-custody for artifacts, and safe fallback actions that preserve service availability.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, actionable run-notes guide for first responders and on-call engineers. It combines signal triage heuristics, RBAC v2 account/session capture steps, audit-log field mapping for SIEM export, and automated evidence orchestration recipes. It's intentionally pragmatic — think "what I need in first 30 minutes".

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to incidents affecting production inference endpoints, control plane, and customer-dedicated clusters.
- Assumes RBAC v2 is active and audit logging is enabled (audit.log service -> central collector).
- SIEM export uses the central delivery pipeline (fluentd -> kafka -> SIEM-ingest).
- Forensic images and raw disk captures handled by SRE with legal sign-off; this doc covers log/evidence capture, not full disk imaging.

High-level triage flow (first 30 min):
1) Signal intake: identify signal source (pager alert / SIEM rule / customer report / telemetry spike). Record: timestamp, channel, observable id (alert id / trace id).
2) Quick impact triage: scope (single user / tenant / region / global), severity (P0/P1/P2), service impact (latency/errors/compromise).
3) Immediate containment if safety-critical: throttle routes, revert recent rollouts, apply deny-list to suspicious tokens. Note: containment must follow RBAC-safe path — avoid mass key rotation unless scoped.
4) Evidence capture (parallel): collect audit entries, session metadata, and configured SIEM extracts (see "Audit fields + export snippet").
5) Notify stakeholders: SEC-OPS, SRE-oncall, owning-service lead, CS if customer-facing. Use the incident channel with the incident id.

Detailed quick checklist (do these in order, mark done):
- [ ] Create incident channel (#sec-incident-<id>) and add stakeholders.
- [ ] Snapshot alert context (alert id, rule name, raw payload).
- [ ] Query audit logs for 5 minutes before and after first observed event.
- [ ] Capture RBAC session context for affected principals (user_id, role_id, session_id, token_id).
- [ ] Export relevant SIEM events to a forensics bucket with write-once retention.
- [ ] If credentials are involved, rotate tokens for the smallest scope possible.
- [ ] Do not delete logs or rotate until evidence copy confirmed.

RBAC v2 mapping and session capture (practical steps):
- Why: RBAC v2 has multi-namespace roles and transient "delegated" sessions. Incidents often require knowing both the principal and the effective policy at time T.
- Capture steps:
  1) From the alert: extract principal id (principal_id). If not present, use trace id to look up request headers in request-index.
  2) Use internal API: GET /rbac/v2/sessions?session_id=<session_id> OR /rbac/v2/principals/<principal_id>/active-sessions to retrieve session metadata.
  3) Record: principal_id, actor_type (service/user), role_bindings (list), effective_permissions (list), delegation_chain (if any), token_id, token_issue_ts. Save a JSON snapshot to the evidence bucket.
- Minimum fields to capture (CSV-friendly): principal_id, principal_name, actor_type, tenant_id, session_id, token_id, roles_assigned, roles_effective, session_start, session_end (if closed), request_ids.

Audit log schema and SIEM export mapping (summary):
- Audit schema canonical fields (our audit-collector normalizes to these names):
  - event_id (uuid)
  - event_ts (ISO8601)
  - source_service (string)
  - env (prod/staging)
  - principal_id
  - principal_type (user/service)
  - tenant_id
  - request_id
  - session_id
  - action (e.g., model.invoke, keys.create, rollout.apply)
  - outcome (success/failure/denied)
  - ip_address
  - user_agent
  - request_payload_hash (sha256)
  - response_status
  - extra (map -> flattened into extra_<k>)

- SIEM export requirements: include at least event_id,event_ts,source_service,principal_id,action,outcome,tenant_id,request_id,session_id,ip_address,raw_message. All exports must be gzip-compressed and signed with delivery signature.

- Example Splunk query (adapt to ours):
  index=redwood_audit action=model.invoke tenant_id=acme-corp | stats count by outcome,principal_id | where outcome="denied"

- Example Elasticsearch DSL snippet for export filter: (plain text for on-call copy)
  {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"env":"prod"}},{"range":{"event_ts":{"gte":"now-5m","lte":"now"}}}]}}}

Automated evidence orchestration recipes (runbook automation):
- Purpose: fast, reproducible capture of relevant artifacts with minimum human error.
- Trigger points: pager alert -> webhook -> evidence-runner job.
- Evidence-runner actions (idempotent):
  1) Pause any automated log pruning for matching tenant for 1 hour.
  2) Archive audit logs for time window [-10m, +30m] to gs://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/audit_logs/ with sha256 manifest.
  3) Snapshot session metadata from RBAC API and save JSON to evidence bucket.
  4) Pull associated traces (trace ids found in audit logs) and store as trace.json.gz.
  5) Generate a minimal chain-of-custody text file: collector_hostname, capture_ts, operator (automated), sha256 sums, signed_by (service account).
  6) Trigger SIEM export job: produce signed package and push to SIEM ingress (internal endpoint) with delivery receipt.
- How to run manual fallback (if automation fails): run ./scripts/manual-evidence-collect.sh <incident-id> on bastion with env=prod. This script performs the same steps with interactive confirmations.

Chain-of-custody and retention notes:
- All evidence artifacts for security incidents are stored in gs://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/ with write-once ACL and 365-day retention by default, unless legal requests different retention.
- Manifest file must include checksums and the automation run id.
- Any change to evidence must be recorded as a new object with a reason header (do not overwrite).

Communications and escalation matrix (quick):
- SEC-OPS owner (during business hours): Aisha Patel (pager) / sec-ops-oncall@redwood.com
- SRE response: SRE-oncall channel.
- Legal/Escalation: notify legal@redwood.com for data exposure potential.
- External comms: Only CSM or Head of Security can post public statements — do not confirm leaked/customer data until validated.

Post-incident actions (initial postmortem checklist):
- Within 24 hours: confirm evidence archive exists and is accessible.
- 48–72 hours: draft a short incident timeline (include RBAC snapshots).
- 7 days: full postmortem with root cause, mitigations, and concrete rollout changes. Attach SIEM export logs and RBAC snapshots.

Common gotchas and quick notes (less formal):
- RBAC session IDs can be ephemeral; if missing, request request_id -> session lookup from the request-index service.
- Some older services still log to legacy_audit; if nothing appears in central audit, check legacy stream before escalating.
- SIEM ingestion failures are rare but possible; always check delivery receipts in kafka/ingest.
- Do NOT mass-rotate keys for an entire tenant unless compromise is confirmed — doing so can cause customer outages.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a stitched playbook for "compromised service account" with step-by-step token revocation for delegated sessions (ticket: JIRA-SEC-4189).
- Centralize a one-click button in console to "freeze and collect" for a tenant (prod UX design needed).
- Validate that evidence bucket retention aligns with EU data residency when incident touches EU tenants.

Appendix: quick commands (for on-call terminal)
- collect audit logs (example):
  $ python infra/tools/export_audit.py --tenant acme-corp --start "2026-03-01T14:00:00Z" --end "2026-03-01T14:40:00Z" --out gs://redwood-evidence/IR-123/audit/
- capture RBAC session snapshot:
  $ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
    "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/rbac/v2/sessions?session_id=abc-123" > session-abc-123.json
- trigger automation run (if webhook missed):
  $ gcloud functions call evidenceRunner --data '{"incident_id":"IR-123","window_mins":40}'

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally concise — keep it light and actionable. Add missing command snippets that you used recently.
- If you see duplicative retention rules across legal and infra, flag to me (Aisha).

End of doc.
